## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 6 (entitled *Upatiṭṭhana*) is a monastic rule of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka that forbids a fully ordained nun from attending upon a monk while he is taking a meal [SuttaCentral; Hüsken 1997]. In the canonical origin story, a nun attends upon a monk—identified as her former husband—while he eats soft food, standing nearby fanning him with one hand and holding a drinking vessel with the other [Hüsken 1997]. The text specifies non-offence clauses (*anāpatti*, Vin IV 264), establishing that no transgression occurs if the food or drink is merely handed over, arranged to be given indirectly, or if an unordained person (such as a female novice, *sāmaṇerī*) is directed to attend on the monk, a distinction discussed also in the commentary *Samantapāsādikā* [Hüsken 1997]. Modern scholarship observes that this rule served both to prevent newly ordained nuns from falling back into subservient domestic roles and to protect nuns against improper demands from monks [Hüsken 1997].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this rule is shared widely across early Buddhist monastic lineages, appearing in the Theravāda Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and Parivāra, as well as the Bhikṣuṇī Vibhaṅgas and Prātimokṣas of the Dharmaguptaka (Pc 75), Mahīśāsaka (Pc 143), Sarvāstivāda (Pc 77), Mūlasarvāstivāda (Pc 78), Mahāsāṅghika (Pc 79), and Lokottaravāda (Pc 79) traditions [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus detects 483 internal Pali text-reuse matches across 108 texts—most extensively with other Vibhaṅga rules such as Bu-Vb Pc 2, Bi-Vb Pc 25, and Bi-Vb Pc 18, as well as the subcommentary *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā*—and identifies machine-calculated cross-language alignments with the Tibetan Vinayavibhaṅga and Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga recensions and a Sanskrit Prātimokṣasūtra [DharmaNexus].
